2026-12-04.title: First Friday of Annunciation · First Friday
2026-12-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Seek the things that are above
2026-12-04.alt: First Friday: devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
2026-12-04.verse: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it.
theo: “If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above… Set your minds on things that are above.” Paul asks the baptised to put to death what is earthly and to “clothe yourselves with the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its creator.”

Jesus tells his disciples that they are blessed: prophets and righteous people longed to see what they see. In the Annunciation season we stand where the prophets longed to stand, at the threshold of the Incarnation. On this First Friday we look at the Heart of the One the prophets longed to see.
outline: Ask: what do your eyes look at most during the day?
Raised with Christ, we set our hearts on heaven.
Point 2 · Put on the new self
Put off the old ways; be renewed in God's image.
We see what prophets longed to see: Christ.
live: Fast from one kind of screen content during these weeks.
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament today.
2026-12-04.prayer: Sacred Heart of Jesus, the prophets longed to see you; I am blessed to know you. Lift my mind to the things above and renew me in your image. Amen.
altar: On First Fridays we honour the Sacred Heart pierced on the Cross. In the Holy Qurbana that same Heart is offered for us, and from it flows the grace that clothes us in the new self.

quick: Seek the things that are above.
Put off the old self; put on the new.
We are blessed to see what prophets longed to see.
2026-12-04.question: What do my eyes seek most?

family.explain: Paul tells us to put on kindness, humility, patience and forgiveness, like clothes we wear every day.
family.intention: We pray for our family on this First Friday, that the Sacred Heart of Jesus may make us kind and forgiving.
family.ask: Ask: “Which ‘clothes’ of kindness will each of us wear this week?”

pm.open: Sacred Heart of Jesus, on this First Friday we gather before you. Open our eyes to see your love and our ears to hear your word, and clothe us with the new life you won for us. Amen.
share: Paul says: seek the things that are above (Colossians 3:1). What earthly worry takes too much of my heart?
Which old garment of sin do I need to take off in confession this Nombu?
Jesus says: blessed are your eyes (Matthew 13:16). How have I seen God at work in my life this year?
pm.resp: Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may always set her heart on Christ and seek the things above.
For sinners, that the love of the Sacred Heart may draw them to confession this season.
For families broken by anger and harsh words, that they may put on kindness and forgiveness.
For those who have lost faith, that their eyes may be opened.
For all who suffer, that they may find rest in the Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, your Heart was pierced for us. Make our hearts like yours: humble, gentle, forgiving. Keep our minds on the things above, and bring us one day to the place you have prepared for us. Amen.

illus: A young man who had stopped going to church came back one First Friday because his mother was ill and had asked him to go in her place. He sat at the back. The Gospel that day said: blessed are your eyes, for they see. He later said: “That day I saw. I went to confession after twelve years.”

homily: Dear friends, on this First Friday of December St Paul lifts our eyes: if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth (Colossians 3:1–2).

This does not mean despising the world. It means ordering our lives. Our houses, jobs, savings and plans are good, but they are not our final home. A person who knows heaven is his home lives differently on earth: more generously, more peacefully, less anxiously.

Then Paul becomes very concrete. Put to death what is earthly in you: sexual immorality, impurity, evil desire and greed. Get rid of anger, wrath, malice, slander and abusive language. Do not lie to one another (Colossians 3:5–9). It is like taking off old, dirty clothes.

And put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its creator (Colossians 3:10). In the old Syriac liturgy, the newly baptised were clothed in white. The Christmas fast is a time to wash those white garments again in confession.

In the Gospel Jesus says to his disciples: blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear; many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it (Matthew 13:16–17). We have what the prophets only dreamed of: the Gospel, the sacraments, the Holy Qurbana, the Church.
Yet we can have eyes and not see. We can hear the Gospel every Sunday and not let it touch us. The First Friday devotion to the Sacred Heart is an invitation to let Christ's love open our eyes.

Today, if possible, make a good confession and receive Holy Communion in honour of the Sacred Heart. Take off one old garment of sin, and ask Jesus to give you eyes that truly see and ears that truly hear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: happy are your eyes, because you can know me! Thank Jesus today that you know Him.

intro: Seek the things above; we see what the prophets longed to see. First Friday: the Sacred Heart.

points.h: The people who walked in darkness
sub: The prophets longed for the light.
The light has come in Christ.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
points.apply: Thank God for the gift of faith.

sub: Many righteous people waited and did not see.
We stand at the threshold of the Incarnation.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.

sub: Raised with Christ, we seek heaven.
The Sacred Heart draws our hearts upward.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Consecrate your family to the Sacred Heart.

concl: We are blessed to see Christ.
Let us set our hearts on him.
